title: Pilot repo decisions
intro: The pilot repo (plaktoz/test-adapters) has rules the spec does not meet yet. Merge policy and the model field are settled in the notes below; these four need your call.
target: docs/design/phase-2.md (P2-4) and the module files it names

decisions.title: Commits the engine makes without a request
decisions.ref: Module 7, checkpoint; the repo's AGENTS.md says no commit without a request
decisions.context: Checkpoints are WIP commits on a task branch. They also drive crash recovery (resume from the last checkpoint), note delivery (restart at a checkpoint) and the D12 reset target. The repo rule forbids committing unless asked.

options.name: Keep checkpoints on a local task branch that is never pushed; only the join commit is pushed
pros: Crash recovery and notes keep working
Task branches are already never pushed in the spec
The pushed history is one commit per task
cons: Still creates local commits the repo rule did not ask for
Needs the owner to accept 'the engine commits locally' as a request

options.name: Turn checkpoints off in this repo; snapshot with a stash or a patch file instead
pros: No commit the owner did not request
cons: A new engine path to build and test for one repo
Recovery and the D12 reset must use patches, which merge badly

options.name: Record the owner's request once in the repo config and treat it as the request for all checkpoint commits
pros: The consent is written down and reviewable
cons: Interprets the repo rule loosely; the owner must agree that it counts

decisions.why: Checkpoints carry three features, so removing them costs more than keeping them local.

decisions.title: Run state and worktrees against the repo's worktree rule
decisions.context: The repo says work stays in the worktree until git status is clean, and a worktree is removed only after a comparison. The engine removes task worktrees right after the join and the run worktree after merge.

options.name: Make cleanup run the repo's comparison first and skip removal when it fails
pros: Leaves a report when it skips
cons: Needs the comparison as a configurable command per repo
Leftover worktrees pile up until someone clears them

options.name: Never remove worktrees in this repo; the owner runs gc by hand
cons: Defeats the end-of-life promise in the spec

decisions.why: The spec already skips dirty worktrees, so one more gate is a small step.

decisions.title: When the pilot starts
decisions.ref: docs/design/phase-2.md P2-4; phase split in the main spec
decisions.context: The repo's open tasks are jest feature work, which needs the 1b feature workflow. A chore or bug-fix pilot could run on phase 1a.

options.name: Start in phase 1a with one chore or bug-fix issue, human merge, then move to feature work in 1b
pros: Real feedback on the core loop early
Tests the repo constraints before feature work
cons: Needs a suitable chore or bug in the repo
Pilot results arrive before the dashboard has writes

options.name: Wait for phase 1b and start with a feature task
pros: One start, no rework of constraints
cons: No real-repo feedback for the whole of 1a

decisions.why: The riskiest assumptions are the repo constraints, and a chore tests them cheaply.

decisions.title: Which model the engine records for this repo
decisions.ref: Module 9 and module 14; the gateway does not allow a chosen model
decisions.context: Workers must not send a model override here. The usage record still needs a model name, and the gateway reports one at run time (this session's own calls report an unrecognized model name).

options.name: Leave model unset, and store whatever the harness result reports as the observed model
pros: Works if the gateway changes model
cons: The name may be an alias such as an internal gateway label
Reports group by an unstable string

options.name: Store a fixed label from repo config, such as 'gateway-default'
cons: Can silently hide a real model change
A guess recorded as a fact

decisions.why: The usage record is for facts, so it keeps what the harness reported.
